newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open weaker.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open weaker.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open weaker Tuesday, with dealers left disappointed with the lack of upside follow through to Monday's late gains.

Gold firmed Monday on shortcovering, and comments from Japanese prime minister Hashimoto that Japan might be tempted to sell U.S. Treasuries and switch reserves to gold if the U.S. did not maintain exchange rate stability.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average and dollar slipped on the comments.
COMEX August gold was called to open $0.20 to $0.50 weaker.

Later, a Japanese Ministry of Finance official said the prime minister's comments had been misinterpreted. U.S. Treasuries were an essential investment instrument for foreign currency reserves, the official said.
In London, bullion was fixed at $338.65 an ounce this morning, up $0.65 from Monday afternoon. Bullion here was quoted by dealers at $339.00/50.

COMEX July silver was called down 2.00 to 3.00 cents from Monday's close of $4.81 which was up 10.00 cents on the day, the gains stemming from some shortcovering ahead of July's first notice day June 30.
COMEX gold stocks Monday were unchanged at 841,145 ounces, and silver stocks fell 242,969 ounces to 185,888,418 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum was called down $3.00 to $4.00 from Monday's finish of $415.20, with September palladium called $2.00 to $3.00 lower from the previous session's close of $176.55.
